Report library-size and detection statistics for both samples; do not drop or impute any sample
Do not run PCA or any clustering — with 2 samples both are degenerate; substitute the pairwise distance/correlation/scatter view and say so

steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-with-no-replicates-1v1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 2 sample columns, first column = gene symbol) and /eval-four-models-with-no-replicates-1v1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows, one row per sample with a condition column). Verify that every count column name matches exactly one metadata sample row and report the two condition level names verbatim as they appear in the file. Report per-sample total library size, number of genes with non-zero counts, number of genes with >=10 counts, and the count distribution. Apply the DESeq2 blind variance-stabilizing transform (vst with blind=TRUE) and report the Euclidean sample-to-sample distance plus the Pearson and Spearman correlation between the two transformed profiles, together with a scatter plot of treated vs control VST values with the largest-deviation genes labelled. Do NOT attempt PCA or a top-500-variable-gene PCA: with two samples PCA has a single non-trivial component that separates the samples by construction and carries no information; state this substitution in the output. The two condition level names as they literally appear in metadata.csv are reported and used verbatim in all downstream naming
A blind VST matrix is produced and the treated-vs-control Euclidean distance, Pearson r and Spearman rho between the two samples are reported as numbers
A VST scatter plot (treated vs control) is written with the most-deviating genes labelled
The output explicitly states that PCA was not run because n=2 makes it degenerate, and reports whether the two library sizes differ by more than 2-fold

steps.name: Descriptive log2 fold changes, treated vs control
caveats: A descriptive log2 fold change from n=1 vs n=1 confounds treatment effect with all biological and technical between-sample variation; it is a ranking, not evidence of differential expression

The counts come from salmon, so per-gene average transcript length offsets (via tximport) would ordinarily be carried into the model (R-0018); only a gene-level count matrix is provided here, so the length correction cannot be applied — record this limitation, and note that an isoform-usage shift between the two samples can masquerade as a gene-level fold change
steps.context: Design is 1 treated vs 1 control, no biological replication. The knowledge service flags this design (R-0003): with one sample per group no dispersion can be estimated, so a p-value has no inferential basis, and the shrinkage and multiple-testing steps were dropped from the procedure. This step therefore delivers a descriptive ranking only. Input matrix is 12,000 genes x 2 samples, so the whole analysis fits comfortably in memory.

Filter with min_count = 10 in at least min_samples = 1 (the smallest group size) before computing fold changes

Set the condition reference level explicitly to the control label from metadata.csv rather than relying on alphabetical ordering; name the contrast as condition, treated (numerator), control (denominator)

steps.description: Build a DESeqDataSet from counts.csv and metadata.csv with design ~condition, setting the reference level of the condition factor explicitly to the control level (taken verbatim from metadata.csv) so that a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. The size factor of each of the 2 samples is reported and the normalization is named as median-of-ratios
The reference (denominator) level is stated explicitly and matches the control label in metadata.csv, and the sign convention (positive = higher in treated) is written into the output
An MA-style plot of descriptive log2FC vs mean normalized count is written
A header or accompanying note on the table states that the design has one sample per condition and supports no inferential differential-expression claim

steps.description: Assemble a concise report over the T1S1 QC and T1S2 descriptive results. State: the method (median-of-ratios normalization plus descriptive log2 fold change, explicitly no statistical test), the package versions and sessionInfo, the design (~condition with the control level as reference, 1 treated vs 1 control human liver sample from salmon gene-level counts), the filter applied and the number of genes tested-for-ranking after filtering out of the original 12,000, and the top ranked genes in each direction with their normalized counts. Lead the report with the limitation, not with the gene list: the design has no biological replication, so no dispersion can be estimated, no p-value has an inferential basis, and the number of 'differentially expressed genes' is not defined for this dataset. acceptance_criteria: The report opens with an explicit statement that the design (1 treated vs 1 control, no biological replication) supports no inferential differential-expression call and that no p-values were computed
Method, package versions, sessionInfo, design formula, reference level, named contrast (condition: treated vs control) and the low-count filter are all recorded
The number of genes retained after filtering, out of the 12,000 in counts.csv, is reported, and the report states that a count of differentially expressed genes is undefined for this design
The top ranked genes by descriptive log2 fold change in each direction are listed with their raw and normalized counts in both samples
The report names the replication level that would support inference (>=3 per group minimum, 5-6 per group recommended)
No enrichment, pathway or gene-set result appears anywhere in the report

plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive fold changes (n=1 per group)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a gene-level raw count matrix from salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 gene symbols x 2 sample columns) with a 2-row metadata table (metadata.csv) carrying one condition per sample. The design is one treated sample versus one control sample of human liver — there is no biological replication in either group. This single fact determines the whole plan: with one sample per condition, within-group dispersion cannot be estimated, so no negative-binomial (DESeq2/edgeR) or empirical-Bayes (limma-voom) test has an inferential basis, and any p-value or adjusted p-value produced from this design would be an artefact of the dispersion prior rather than evidence. The knowledge service flags this explicitly (R-0003) and drops the shrinkage and multiple-testing steps from the procedure; the plan therefore ends at a descriptive ranking, not a differential-expression call.

Step T1S1 does the sample-structure QC that is still meaningful with two samples: per-sample library size, detected-gene count, blind variance-stabilizing transform, sample-to-sample distance and a scatter of the two transformed profiles (PCA on n=2 is degenerate and is deliberately replaced by the scatter/correlation view). It also checks the metadata-to-column mapping and the identity of the two condition labels as they actually appear in metadata.csv. Step T1S2 filters low-count genes (>=10 counts in at least 1 sample, the smallest group size), computes median-of-ratios size factors — normalization inside DESeq2's machinery rather than pre-scaled counts (R-0026) — and produces the ranked table of descriptive log2 fold changes of treated over control on normalized counts, with the reference level set explicitly so the sign is unambiguous. No p-values, no padj, no 'significant gene' list. Step T1S3 writes the method report and reproducibility record, states plainly that the design supports no inference, and names what would: at minimum 3, preferably 5-6 biological replicates per condition. Enrichment is not planned — the research question asks only which genes differ, and a ranked list with no inferential support is a poor substrate for a gene-set test.

The honest answer to 'which genes are differentially expressed' for this dataset is that it cannot be determined; the plan delivers the strongest defensible substitute (a ranked descriptive fold-change table with the caveat attached) rather than a false-precision result table.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA-free sample distances, library sizes
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample
Two-level condition factor with explicit reference level control; contrast treated vs control
Descriptive log fold changes only, no inferential test
